page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-96GB is a Cloud Native virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities alongside weak single-core execution. The stress-ng single-core CPU test places in the bottom 10%, while multi-core performance falls within the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, as well as PassMark memory and database operations, consistently rank in the average tier. However, image processing and medium-model LLM inference show weaker performance, placing in the bottom 25%.

Given its shared CPU allocation and high memory density, this server offers a cost-effective profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated single-core CPU performance. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis, text processing, and general-purpose web serving where memory capacity is prioritized over raw compute power.
